lines: Lesson six. Commands.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
This is how you stop typing the same prompt every day.

scenes.headline: Same prompt again? Make it a command.
scenes.sub: Type a slash and a word.
lines: If you keep pasting the same prompt, it's time for a command.
Type a slash and a word, and the whole prompt runs.
Add a word after it, to point it at what matters today.

callout.t: One file. One word. Same result every time.
callout.label: Slash command

scenes.headline: Three parts. Six lines.
lines: Here's a review command.
Frontmatter at the top describes it.
A slot catches whatever you type after the command.
And the body is just the prompt.
scenes.code:
---
description: Review staged changes
argument-hint: [focus area]
---
Review `git diff --staged`.
Focus on: $ARGUMENTS
List bugs first, then style nits.

scenes.headline: Same idea. Different folder.
lines: Each harness calls them something slightly different.
Commands, prompts, or workflows. Same idea, different folder.

scenes.headline: Keep commands in git.
lines: Keep them in git.
Write one file per command.
Commit it next to the code.
And the whole team gets it on their next pull.

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
A command is a saved prompt, with frontmatter, arguments, and a body.
Your mission: turn the prompt you paste most often into a slash command, and commit it.
